History of the Internet

The Internet has its roots in the Cold War and was initially developed as a way to maintain communications in the event of a nuclear attack. In the late 1960s, the Advanced Research Projects Agency Network (ARPANET) was created by the U.S. Department of Defense as a way to share information over a network. ARPANET was the precursor to the modern Internet as we know it today.

The concept of hypertext, the basis for the World Wide Web, was developed in the 1960s and 1970s. In the late 1980s, the National Science Foundation (NSF) established the NSFNET, which expanded the Internet beyond military and academic institutions. By the 1990s, the Internet began to grow exponentially, thanks to the commercialization of the Internet and the development of the World Wide Web.
